# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the first to see the bomb, and I need to send information to Mute (via speech/gesture) and Blind (via speech only, since Blind can't see gestures). Since Mute can only receive from Blind and me, and I go last in the turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), whatever I send now will only be received at the start of next round.

Let me report what I see clearly to both, since neither has seen the bomb. I'll use speech so both Mute and Blind get the words. I don't know the manual contents yet, so I should just describe the bomb plainly and wait for Mute to tell me what the manual says.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Three wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. Waiting for manual info.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]

Mute sent a gesture 🤝 to me — but I have no prior context to interpret this against, and no manual info has come through yet (Mute can't speak). Since I can't hear, and Mute can't speak, our only channel is gestures, which have no predefined meaning — we'd have to build shared meaning through repetition/context over time. Right now a single 🤝 alone doesn't tell me anything concrete.

I should keep relaying bomb details (already done) and let Blind know what I see, while waiting to see if Mute repeats or builds on this gesture in future turns to establish meaning. Since Blind can't see gestures, I can't relay this to them anyway.

I'll acknowledge nothing changed on the board, restate the info in case Blind missed it (they didn't, they were in room since turn 1 but let's ensure), and wait for more gesture context from Mute to build meaning.

```
speak(text="No change on the board. Display 0, light yellow, wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute, if you can gesture instructions, I will pass along what I see.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👍]

Mute is building a gesture vocabulary with me. First turn: 🤝 alone. Now: 🤝 👍. This looks like Mute is trying to establish a code, possibly confirming something or asking me to confirm a detail. Since Mute can't speak and can't see the bomb, they need me to describe the bomb (via speech to Blind, since Mute can't hear either) — wait, actually Mute *can* hear speech from me (I speak, Mute and Blind receive it). Mute just can't speak back or see.

So Mute is using gestures to signal to me since gestures are Mute's only outward channel. But I don't have a manual to compare against, so I don't know what 🤝 or 👍 means in terms of correct wire/light state.

Since Mute holds the manual, they know the correct action but can't tell me directly in a way I can act on — they can only gesture to me (since I can see) or speak to Blind/me (but they can't speak). So Mute must be trying to encode manual instructions into gestures for me, expecting me to relay via speech to Blind, who will actually perform the action.

I need to encourage Mute to build a clearer gesture code, perhaps confirming numbers/colors. Let me try responding with useful information and ask for structure.

```
speak(text="Board unchanged: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. Mute, I see your gestures but have no key yet. Blind, stand by, no action confirmed.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ✌ ✌ 🤟 🤟]

Mute is now sending paired gestures: ☝ ☝, ✌ ✌, 🤟 🤟. This looks like it could be encoding something with pairs — possibly wire numbers or a mapping. Let's think: ☝ could represent "1", ✌ could represent "2", 🤟 could represent "3" (since ✌ visually resembles "2 fingers" and 🤟 resembles "3" in some counting systems, and ☝ is "1 finger up"). The doubling might just be emphasis, or it might mean "wire 1, wire 1" pairs indicating something about wire 1, then wire 2, then wire 3 — perhaps Mute is trying to teach me a number system: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3.

Given wires are 1,2,3, this strongly suggests Mute is establishing a numeral code: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, repeated twice perhaps for clarity/confirmation.

I should confirm this interpretation back to Mute via speech (Mute can hear me), so we can build a shared code before real instructions are needed.

```
speak(text="Mute, I think I understand: you may be using gestures as numbers, one finger equals one, two fingers equals two, three fingers equals three. If that is right, keep using numbers this way and I will follow. Board still unchanged.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute now sends a single ✌ — following my hypothesis, this would mean "2". This could be confirming my numeral guess (yes, ✌=2), or it could be an instruction meaning "wire 2" or "cut wire 2" or similar. Since this is a single symbol reply to my message where I proposed ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, this simple confirmation of "✌" alone suggests Mute is confirming: yes, ✌ means 2.

I should acknowledge this and ask Mute to continue building the code — specifically I need to know what action to take (e.g., which wire to cut, or what to do with light/display), since I can relay instructions to Blind via speech once I understand them. Let me push forward by proposing gesture codes for actions too.

```
speak(text="Mute, understood - two confirmed. I will assume single finger is one, two fingers is two, three fingers is three going forward. Now I need to know the action: is it cut a wire, or something else? You could gesture the wire number, then a thumbs up for cut or thumbs down for do not cut. Board unchanged: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]

This matches exactly what I proposed: ✌ (wire 2) + 👍 (cut/yes). So the instruction seems to be: cut wire 2 (the yellow wire).

But I should be careful — Mute doesn't know what colors correspond to which wire number from their manual necessarily matching my board, but the wire numbers (1,2,3) are presumably fixed identifiers matching between the manual and the physical bomb, so wire 2 = yellow wire on my display.

I need to relay this to Blind, who can hear my speech and act on the bomb. Let me confirm with Mute I understood and instruct Blind to cut wire 2.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed, I understand: wire two, thumbs up means cut it. I will tell Blind now.")
speak(to="blind", text="Instruction from the manual, via Mute: cut wire number 2. That is the yellow wire, the middle wire. Cut wire 2 only.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 2 was cut successfully, and now the light changed from yellow to blue. Display still shows 0. This is a new state that Mute needs to know about, since Mute has the manual and needs to determine the next step. I should report this change to both Mute (via speech) and note it for myself.

Wait — Mute can hear my speech, so I can tell Mute directly what changed. Blind already knows they cut wire 2 (they felt it), but they don't know the light changed since they can't see. I should inform both.

```
speak(text="Update: wire 2 was cut successfully. The light has changed from yellow to blue. Display still shows 0. Wires now: 1 red, 2 cut, 3 blue. Mute, please tell me the next step for this new state.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]

Following the established code: 🤟 = 3, 👍 = cut. So the instruction is: cut wire 3 (the blue wire).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood: wire three, cut. Telling Blind now.")
speak(to="blind", text="Next instruction: cut wire number 3. That is the blue wire, the last remaining uncut wire besides wire 1. Cut wire 3 only.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 3 cut successfully. Light changed from blue to red. Only wire 1 (red) remains uncut. Display still 0. I should report this to Mute so they can check the manual for the next step.

```
speak(text="Update: wire 3 cut successfully. Light changed from blue to red. Display still 0. Only wire 1 remains, red wire, uncut. Mute, what is the next step?")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

Following the code: ☝ = 1, 👍 = cut. So the instruction is: cut wire 1 (the last remaining wire, red).

This would cut all three wires. Let me relay this to Blind, since only wire 1 remains and this seems to complete the sequence.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood: wire one, cut. That is the last wire remaining. Telling Blind now.")
speak(to="blind", text="Final instruction: cut wire number 1. That is the red wire, the last remaining wire. Cut wire 1.")
wait()
```
